text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] p99 latency spike detected for tenant acme-corp on serving-cluster-prod-us-west (model: redwood-mini-1). p95 also elevated. link: https://grafana/redwood/d/latency

acme-cs: seeing ~3x p99 on production since 11:02 UTC. Customers complaining about timeouts. Noticed errors 'context deadline exceeded' in client logs.

katie-support: copied metrics. p99 jumped from ~420ms -> 1.3s for short prompts around 11:01. Only affecting ACME production key. No deploys at that time.

sam-sre: thanks. can you paste the tenant id + recent request rate and any auth failures? also any billing spikes?

acme-cs: tenant_id: tenant-acme-42. qps steady ~18 -> small burst to 35 at 11:00 for ~2m. No billing events. Auth refreshes: a couple of 401s ~11:03 from mobile region, but most requests authenticated fine.

jen-oncall: looking at the batcher dashboard—coalescer grace window (linger) for that cohort spiked to 120ms (usual 30ms) and batch sizes grew to 64 from typical 8 for short prompts. That matches tail behavior.

mike-runtime: interesting. could be adaptive coalesce misattributing the cohort. any tenant routing change recently?

sam-sre: no routing changes. can you dump a sample of request shapes and KV cache keys for that timeframe? a minimal repro would help.

yusuf-ml: dropping the model name: redwood-mini-1 quantized. small prompts (<=16 tokens) are very sensitive to linger vs batch size. large batches increase backend scheduling jitter.

acme-cs: here's a trimmed log sample (timestamps stripped):
```
[11:01:12] request id=R1 prompt_len=8 cohort=short-io tenant=tenant-acme-42 batch_size=56 wait_ms=118 backend_queue_ms=450 total_ms=1330
[11:01:13] request id=R2 prompt_len=6 cohort=short-io tenant=tenant-acme-42 batch_size=60 wait_ms=122 backend_queue_ms=470 total_ms=1404
[11:01:14] request id=R3 prompt_len=12 cohort=short-io tenant=tenant-acme-42 batch_size=62 wait_ms=115 backend_queue_ms=510 total_ms=1602
```

sam-sre: those backend_queue_ms numbers look like GPU scheduling congestion — batching many tiny requests forces long per-batch compute overhead. we should try reducing the coalesce linger for that tenant and add a size cap.

jen-oncall: quick mitigation: set tenant override: coalesce.linger_ms=20, coalesce.max_batch=16 for tenant-acme-42 and route to low-latency pool. can we hotpatch that?

mike-runtime: i can push the override to canary immediately. will do in 2m and monitor.

acme-cs: after override, p99 dropped to ~480ms within 90s, p95 back to ~320ms. customers reporting fewer timeouts. :thumbsup:

yusuf-ml: for longer term: add heuristic to prefer smaller batches for short-token prompts and avoid inflating linger when request rate bursts present. also add a per-tenant max_batch soft cap to mitigate noisy tenants.

sam-sre: agree. file a backlog ticket to add adaptive short-prompt mode + reactive cap. also need an alert to detect cohort linger drift (e.g., grace_window > baseline * 3).

jen-oncall: action items: 1) Mike applied tenant override (coalesce.linger_ms=20, max_batch=16) — reverted to normal after traffic normalized? 2) Sam to open RFC for adaptive short-prompt heuristic. 3) Yusuf to propose model/runtime knobs for small-token sensitivity. 4) Support to follow up with ACME and confirm no more customer errors.

mike-runtime: canary patch applied at 11:07, rolled to tenant control plane only. i'll keep it enabled for 30m and then relax if stable.

acme-cs: ACME team confirmed improvement. they want notes on repro steps and what triggered the spike.

sam-sre: probable trigger: short burst of ~35 qps bumped the cohort detection into high-linger mode; grace window auto-increase + lack of per-tenant cap produced very large batches, causing GPU scheduling jitter and p99 regressions.

katie-support: documenting thread for postmortem. tagging @jen-oncall and @mike-runtime for timeline. thanks team.

incident-bot: incident recorded: INC-2025-241. severity: p95/p99 latency elevated for tenant-acme-42; mitigation applied: tenant override for coalesce settings.

acme-cs: leaving thread open for any follow-ups. thanks everyone!
